newsitem.title: USA: Genentech, Boehringer drugs seen comparable.
newsitem.headline: Genentech, Boehringer drugs seen comparable.

text.p: Genentech Inc's new heart attack drug, t-PA, was shown to be comparable to Boehringer Mannheim Corp's r-PA, or Retavase, according to a study by the Cleveland Clinic's Department of Cardiology.
The study results were reported Monday at the American College of Cardiology meeting here.
The study involved patients being treated for myocardial infarction and found that those given r-PA were "statistically no more likely to die within 30 days than patients treated with t-PA."

Specifically the study showed that 7.43 percent of the r-PA patients died within 30 days, compared with 7.22 percent of t-PA patients. The rate of stroke was 1.67 percent in the r-PA patients, compared with 1.83 percent in t-PA patients; and the rate of intracranial hemorrhage was 0.91 percent in r-PA patients compared with 0.88 percent in t-PA patients.
